To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the high voltage capability of silicon detector diodes is limited by the junction edge field.
the high-voltage capability of detector diode junctions can be increased by increasing the junction depth.

(1) the high voltage capability of planar detector diodes is limited by the junction depth, (2) increasing the junction depth increases the breakdown voltage, and (3) the breakdown voltage is in reasonable agreement with the predictions of previous studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the junction depth dependence of the breakdown voltage of detector diodes.
the development of a new type of radiation detector based on silicon diodes.
the study of the junction depth dependence of the high field breakdown voltage in silicon detector diode structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the junction depth is the most critical parameter in determining the breakdown voltage of a silicon detector diode.
junction breakdown is not the dominant factor in determining the breakdown voltage in planar detector diodes.
, for a given junction depth, the breakdown voltage is not significantly dependent on the junction area, but that for a given junction area, the breakdown voltage does depend on the junction depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the breakdown voltage increases with junction depth, but is not linear.
a 1.5 times higher junction depth leads to a 2.5 times higher breakdown voltage, while a ten times higher junction depth results in a 100 times higher breakdown voltage.
the junction depth is the key to high voltage capability of silicon detector diodes, with a junction depth of 5 μm being sufficient for operation at 200 V.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the breakdown voltage of detector diodes can be increased without sacrificing the signal-to-noise ratio by simply increasing the junction depth.
junction breakdown is a function of both junction depth and surface field.
the high field at the edge of a junction is not the only limiting factor to breakdown.
